h: לַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב, א׳ Tu B'Av, 1

p: "There were no festive days for Yisrael
like the fifteenth of Av," etc.
עַל מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים כָּזֶה.
for why there were no festive days like it.
But where do we find an allusion in the Torah
לָזֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב יוֹם טוֹב?
to this, that the fifteenth of Av is called a Yom Tov?
that it comes from what is said (Shoftim 21:19):
"Behold, there is a festival of Hashem in Shiloh
"and behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out
to dance in the dances," etc. (ibid. 21:21).
Now it does not specify which festival it is
and the Radak explained it as Yom Kippur,
"and the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out
that Yom Kippur is called a chag?
Rather, it is called only "a holy convocation,"
for only the three Regalim are called chag:
For chag is a term of rejoicing
which is why in the language of Chazal
which is the season of our rejoicing.
chag as a term of dancing,
as in "they reel and stagger like a drunkard" (Tehillim 107:27) —
there too it is a term of rejoicing,
for the drunkard, from the wine,
his heart is glad within him.
And so it is written (Shmuel I 30:16):
meaning that they were rejoicing in the spoil
And dancing too is included in it,
and it is forced to say
that it alludes to Yom Kippur.
that "a festival of Hashem in Shiloh," etc.,
is meant for the fifteenth of Av.
which is the season of our rejoicing,
and about which the mitzvah of rejoicing is written explicitly;
it is written "and you shall rejoice in your festival" (Devarim 16:14),
that is, the rejoicing of Yisrael,
in remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt.
We find it in the Torah only with Aharon,
who said "Tomorrow shall be a festival to Hashem" (Shemos 32:5)
when the first forty days were completed
שֶׁהָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּהָר,
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was on the mountain,
and he had said that then he would come down from the mountain
with the two Luchos in his hand.
And were it not for the corruption,
it would then have been "a festival to Hashem,"
for then it was meant to be
the day of the gladness of the heart
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
And as it was said in Egypt:
that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness" (Shemos 5:1),
that Yisrael made a festival in the wilderness.
And if it refers to the festivals,
the three Regalim that they kept —
Chag HaMatzos in Egypt as well.
Rather, "that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness"
And had there been no corruption of the Golden Calf,
and had the Luchos not been broken,
then the seventeenth of Tammuz would have been
which is the day of the gladness of His heart,
for then there would have been fulfilled
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ חֲזַ״ל (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה לב, א)
עַל פָּסוּק ״חָרוּת עַל הַלּוּחוֹת״ (שְׁמוֹת לב, טז):
on the pasuk "engraved upon the Luchos" (Shemos 32:16):
freedom from the Angel of Death
and from the subjugation of the kingdoms;
and the words of Torah would have been engraved
there was expounded regarding Yom Kippur,
שֶׁהוּא יוֹם שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ בּוֹ לוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת,
the day on which the second Luchos were given,
the pasuk "on the day of his wedding,"
דְּלֹא הָיָה חָרוּת וְנֶחְקָק בַּלֵּב כָּל כָּךְ
for it was not so engraved and inscribed upon the heart
And "on the day of the gladness of his heart"
was expounded regarding the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days,
for only then will everything be rectified.
וְהִנֵּה הַמֵּימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
Now, the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel cited above
"When Av enters, we diminish in rejoicing;
שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ״
the week in which Tishah B'Av falls,"
from Rosh Chodesh until the fast;
Rabbi Yehudah says the whole month;
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
And all three expounded one verse,
"And I will cause all her joy to cease,
her festival, her new moon, and her Sabbath."
מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית — מֵ״חַגָּהּ״.
The one who says from Rosh Chodesh until the fast derives it from "her festival."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״קָרָא עָלַי מוֹעֵד״ (אֵיכָה א, טו).
as it is said, "He has proclaimed a set time against me" (Eichah 1:15).
But in truth this is difficult to understand,
דְּלֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁנִּקְרָא רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ חַג,
for we do not find that Rosh Chodesh is called chag,
Rosh Chodesh, which is called mo'ed —
let us say Hallel on it!
It is not sanctified by the prohibition of labor,
as in the night when a festival is sanctified" (Yeshayahu 30:29);
a night sanctified as a festival requires song,
וְשֶׁאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁ לְחַג אֵין טָעוּן שִׁירָה.
and one not sanctified as a festival does not require song.
הֲרֵי דְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא חַג,
We see that Rosh Chodesh is not called chag,
for if it were sanctified as a festival,
they would recite the complete Hallel on it.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּ״חַגָּהּ״ קָאֵי עַל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב,
And it seems that "her festival" refers to Tishah B'Av,
which in the time of the Beis HaMikdash was a festival,
"And I will turn your festivals into mourning" (Amos 8:10).
Now which festival was turned into mourning?
If it refers to the five festivals,
surely they were not turned into mourning
any more than the rest of the days of the year.
Rather, it refers to Tishah B'Av,
which in the time of the Beis HaMikdash was a festival.
Just as in the Second Beis HaMikdash
they asked whether they should fast on the fast days,
"The fast of the fourth month," etc.,
"shall be for the house of Yehudah
אַף שֶׁיָּדְעוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא הָיְתָה הַגְּאוּלָּה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
Even though they knew that the redemption was not yet complete,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת הָיָה יוֹם טוֹב,
nevertheless in the time of the Beis HaMikdash it was a Yom Tov,
because they had been fasts beforehand,
וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּדְעוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לְמוֹעֲדִים טוֹבִים.
and because they knew that in the future they would become happy festivals.
So too in the time of the First Beis HaMikdash,
הָיָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב יוֹם טוֹב וּמוֹעֵד,
Tishah B'Av was a Yom Tov and a festival.
וְאַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עוֹד צוֹם מִקּוֹדֶם,
And although it had not yet been a fast beforehand,
nevertheless, from the time of the wilderness
when it was decreed through the Spies,
I will establish for you a weeping for generations."
And in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 16:20) it says:
it was decreed upon the Beis HaMikdash that it be destroyed,
so that Yisrael would go into exile,
"And He lifted His hand against them
to cast them down in the wilderness,
and to cast down their seed among the nations
and to scatter them in the lands" (Tehillim 106:26–27).
And it seems that this refers to the two Destructions:
"to cast down their seed among the nations"
refers to the Destruction of the First Beis HaMikdash,
when it was enough to be in Bavel;
and "to scatter them in the lands"
is the Destruction of the Second Beis HaMikdash,
in which it was decreed to scatter them in the lands,
that they be subjugated to the seventy nations,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב, ח):
"Did not the Holy One, blessed be He, already swear
that He would subjugate us to seventy nations?"
it is as though all of you were exiled."
that they were in Eretz Yisrael,
and only "to cast them down in the wilderness" had been fulfilled,
while they were dwelling in Eretz Yisrael,
לָכֵן עָשׂוּ אָז בִּזְמַן בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן
therefore they made, in the time of the First Beis HaMikdash,
a festival on Tishah B'Av as well,
just as they did in the Second Beis HaMikdash,
when the fast was turned to joy and gladness.
And about this it is said,
"And I will turn your festivals into mourning" —
And it seems that the festival lasted seven days,
מִתִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב עַד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב.
from Tishah B'Av until the fifteenth of Av.
And one may say that this is
שֶׁלָּמְדוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ, א) לַאֲבֵילוּת שִׁבְעָה,
what they derived (Moed Katan 20a) for seven days of mourning,
as it is written, "And I will turn your festivals into mourning":
just as a festival is seven days,
so too mourning is seven days.
like the eight days of the festival!
Shemini is a festival in its own right.
And one may say that in our Gemara they derived it
from what is written, "your festivals into mourning,"
דְּהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לָהֶם תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
that is, Tishah B'Av, which they had
as a seven-day festival in the time of the Beis HaMikdash;
"I will turn your festivals into mourning,"
and from this they derived seven days of mourning.
וּבֶאֱמֶת אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל (תַּעֲנִית ל, ב)
And indeed it says in the Gemara cited above (Taanis 30b),
בֵּין הַטְּעָמִים שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב:
among the reasons for the fifteenth of Av:
the day on which the dead of the wilderness came to an end,
Until the dead of the wilderness came to an end,
לֹא הָיָה דִּבּוּר עִם מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵּי,
there was no Divine speech with Moshe, etc.,
to me was the Divine speech.
Now according to Rashi's explanation in Taanis (30b)
they did not die in the fortieth year.
דְּבַשָּׁנָה אַחֲרוֹנָה גַּם כֵּן מֵתוּ בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב,
that in the last year too they died on Tishah B'Av,
only that because of the mourning,
מִתִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב עַד מִקְצָת יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב,
from Tishah B'Av until part of the day of the fifteenth of Av,
and part of the day counts as the whole —
therefore the Divine speech did not come
which is a term of affection,
כְּמוֹ ״פָּנִים בְּפָנִים דִּבֶּר ה׳ עִמָּכֶם״ (דְּבָרִים ה, ד),
as in "Face to face Hashem spoke with you" (Devarim 5:4),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מַכּוֹת י, ב – יא, א):
and as they said in the Gemara (Makkos 10b–11a):
מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶאֶמְרָה פָּרָשַׁת רוֹצְחִים בִּלְשׁוֹן עַזָּה,
Why was the passage of the killers stated in harsh language,
דִּכְתִיב ״וַיְדַבֵּר ה׳ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ״ וְכוּלֵּי (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כ, א)?
as it is written, "And Hashem spoke to Yehoshua," etc. (Yehoshua 20:1)?
Because they are of the Torah.
For all the words of the Torah
as in "Face to face Hashem spoke with you."
וְלָכֵן עָשׂוּ יוֹם טוֹב בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב,
Therefore they made a Yom Tov on the fifteenth of Av,
for then Hashem spoke to him
(as is written in Rashi's commentary there),
כְּמוֹ ״פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ״ (בְּמִדְבַּר יב, ח).
as in "Mouth to mouth I speak with him" (Bamidbar 12:8).
And therefore they derived seven days of mourning
from what is said, "And I will turn your festivals into mourning,"
which drew along with it seven days
until the fifteenth of the month.
וּבַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ קָבְעוּ בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת
And on its fifteenth, in the time of the Beis HaMikdash, they established
for it was the last day
when the mourning in the wilderness had already ended,
they made a Yom Tov and dances.
And according to this is resolved
"her festival, her new moon, and her Sabbath" according to all the opinions.
For according to Rashi's explanation it is difficult:
for the one who says the whole month,
what did he expound from "her festival" and "her Sabbath"?
גַּם לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ עַד הַתַּעֲנִית,
Also for the one who says from Rosh Chodesh until the fast,
if he expounded "her festival" as Rosh Chodesh,
as in Rashi's explanation cited above,
from where does he derive "until the fast"?
Perhaps only on Rosh Chodesh itself!
But according to what we said, it is resolved:
דִּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ עַד הַתַּעֲנִית
for the one who says from Rosh Chodesh until the fast
וְהוּא דָּרַשׁ ״חָדְשָׁהּ״ עַל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אָב,
And he expounded "her new moon" as Rosh Chodesh Av,
between Rosh Chodesh and the fast.
And the one who says the entire month
and automatically it contains "her festival" as well,
וּמַאן דְּאָמַר כָּל הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר
And the one who says the entire week is forbidden
and he expounded "her festival" and "her new moon"
as referring to the whole year,
כְּמוֹ ״חָדְשֵׁיכֶם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם שָׂנְאָה נַפְשִׁי״ (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יד).
as in "Your new moons and your festivals My soul hates" (Yeshayahu 1:14).
But Shabbos is not mentioned there,
for Shabbos is fixed and established
by the holiness of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, ב):
as is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 88b):
"But Shabbos it does not mention," etc.
And "her Sabbath" refers to the days of the week
שֶׁל הַשָּׁבוּעַ שֶׁחָל בּוֹ תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב.
of the week in which Tishah B'Av falls.
״שִׁכַּח ה׳ בְּצִיּוֹן מוֹעֵד וְשַׁבָּת״ (אֵיכָה ב, ו),
"Hashem has caused festival and Shabbos to be forgotten in Tziyon" (Eichah 2:6),
where Shabbos is mentioned as well —
there it refers to the offerings,
the Mussaf offerings of festival and Shabbos,
through the offerings that Yisrael bring,
Why are the festivals in Bavel joyous?
Because they were not included in that curse,
as it is written, "And I will cause to cease," etc.,
and it is written, "Your new moons and your festivals," etc.
But regarding Sabbaths it is not mentioned
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הֶבְדֵּל בֵּין אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבָבֶל,
that there is any difference between Eretz Yisrael and Bavel;
רַק הַקְּלָלָה הָיָה רַק עַל הַחַגִּים וַחֲדָשִׁים,
rather, the curse was only on the festivals and new moons,
as it is said, "Your new moons and your festivals."
And although in the pasuk "And I will cause to cease" that it cites
one may say that it follows the one who says
the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
"There were no festive days for Yisrael
like the fifteenth of Av," etc.,
'Go out and see, O daughters of Tziyon,
with the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding
וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ׳״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ג, יא).
and on the day of the gladness of his heart'" (Shir HaShirim 3:11).
the King to Whom peace belongs;
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him" —
Now what connection does this have
going out and dancing in the vineyards,
which is taught in the Mishnah just before this?
וּבַגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית לא, א) דָּרְשׁוּ עַל זוֹ הַמֵּימְרָא:
And in the Gemara (Taanis 31a) they expounded on this statement:
The Rabbis taught: The beautiful ones, etc.;
עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מָחוֹל וְכוּלֵּי.
In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance, etc.
And it seems that it is all one,
for "machol" is a term of encircling,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י (תַּעֲנִית לא, א):
as is written in Rashi's commentary (Taanis 31a):
"around," a term from the circling of the vineyards.
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him" —
הַיְינוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם שְׁנֵי כְּתָרִים,
means that Yisrael have two crowns:
the tefillin of the arm and of the head.
correspond to the crown of "we will do,"
for action belongs to the hands,
and they are bound in service to the mitzvos of Hashem.
And the tefillin of the head
correspond to the crown of "we will hear,"
for it corresponds to the brain,
And corresponding to them they said (Berachos 6a)
that Hashem, blessed be He, puts on tefillin,
for He is praised through the praise of Yisrael.
And from the crown of "we will hear,"
כִּבְיָכוֹל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
as it were, Hashem, blessed be He, puts on the tefillin of the head,
and from the crown of "we will do," the tefillin of the arm.
And this is the meaning of
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him":
with "we will do and we will hear."
וְאִם לֹא הָיוּ נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ לוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
And had the first Luchos not been broken,
then the seventeenth of Tammuz would have been
יוֹם חֲתוּנָּתוֹ וְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ יַחַד.
the day of his wedding and the day of the gladness of his heart together.
And after the corruption took place,
then Yom Kippur was called "the day of his wedding,"
for it was then a day of pardon and forgiveness,
and then was repaired what they had corrupted in "we will do"
through the deed of the Golden Calf
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה, עֵקֶב; דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ג, י).
(as is written in the Midrash Rabbah, Eikev; Devarim Rabbah 3:10).
"And the day of the gladness of his heart" —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,

that the words of Torah enter the heart,
and when the heart becomes straight,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה״ (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא),
as it is said, "and for the upright in heart, gladness" (Tehillim 97:11);
And it seems that this is the seventh reason
שֶׁהִתְחִיל הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
that the rectification had begun through Torah she'b'al peh,
one must from then on add time from the night for learning.
וְכֵן כָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (הִלְכוֹת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה ג, יג)
And so wrote the Rambam (Hilchos Talmud Torah 3:13),
One who wishes to merit the crown of Torah
should be careful with all his nights,
and not lose even one of them
וּבָזֶה יוּנַח מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים
And with this we can settle what is written in Pri Etz Chaim,
that there are seven reasons in the Gemara,
although in the Gemara before us there are
רַק שִׁשָּׁה טְעָמִים עַל חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב.
only six reasons for the fifteenth of Av.
But what they said in the Gemara,
"From here on, one who adds will have added to him,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִסְדַּר בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית לא, א):
The Rabbis taught: The beautiful ones among them, etc.
In the Gemara the reading is three groups:
the beautiful, the well-born, the unattractive.
And in Ein Yaakov it counts four groups:
the beautiful, the well-born, the wealthy, and the poor.
And it says in Pri Etz Chaim
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ״ה.
that they correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah.
And this is what they said:
וּרְאֵה מָה אַתָּה בּוֹרֵר לָךְ״ וְכוּלֵּי (תַּעֲנִית כו, ב),
and see what you are choosing for yourself," etc. (Taanis 26b),
which refers to Hashem, blessed be He,
correspond to the final hei of the Holy Name,
as is set out in Shir HaShirim
all the praises of Knesses Yisrael:
with the twenty-four ornaments of a bride,
The well-born correspond to the vav of the Holy Name,
for the essential lineage of Yisrael
is that they are children of Hashem,
"You are children of Hashem your God" (Devarim 14:1).
And this is only in Yaakov,
for there was no dross at all among his offspring.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק,
This is not so with the offspring of Avraham and Yitzchak;
אַף שֶׁהֵם בְּעַצְמָם גַּם כֵּן זָכוּ שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
even though they themselves also merited to be called Yisrael
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סג, ג),
(as is written in the Midrash, Bereishis Rabbah 63:3),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא מִזַּרְעָם פְּסוֹלֶת,
nevertheless, since dross came forth from their offspring,
the name "children of Hashem" cannot apply to them.
Only the offspring of Yaakov — this is the lineage;
and this corresponds to the vav of the Name,
which corresponds to Yaakov, who is called "son,"
which is the aspect of vav and hei.
And this is "Set your eyes on family."
And the wealthy, of whom they said there
that they bring in everything from their own,
this corresponds to the first hei.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כה, ב):
And it is in the manner of what they said (Bava Basra 25b):
"And one who wishes to become wealthy should face north,"
meaning that he should hold fast to and strive in the trait of fear,
which is the aspect of north,
וְהוּא מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
and it is the trait of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה בְּכוֹחוֹ לְקַבֵּל עֲשִׁירוּת,
and through this he will be able to receive wealth,
as it is said of Yitzchak,
which is wealth in great abundance.
And as we heard from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitz,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
״וְאַבְרָם כָּבֵד מְאוֹד בַּמִּקְנֶה״ וְגוֹמֵר (בְּרֵאשִׁית יג, ב):
"And Avram was very heavy with cattle," etc. (Bereishis 13:2):
"heavy" is meant in the sense of "a heavy burden,"
for wealth was to him a yoke and a burden,
in the aspect of love for Hashem, blessed be He,
and he feared for his soul
because of foreign loves that are not in holiness.
But Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose essence was in the aspect of fear,
and was able to receive the wealth.
And fear comes chiefly from the side of man,
"What does Hashem your God ask of you
of those who bring in everything from their own.
in the Gemara the reading is "the unattractive,"
one is poor only in understanding;
and from this it follows that they are unattractive in their deeds.
And this corresponds to the yud of the Holy Name,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם קְשׁוּרִין בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
meaning that nevertheless they are bound at the root
which is the thorn-tip of the yud,
which is the joining of Chochmah and Binah.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא, יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא.
Even though he sinned, he is a Yisrael.
And because of this they are called
and this corresponds to one poor in understanding.
And they say, "provided you adorn me with gold coins,"
meaning that they should give them jewelry,
and then they will not be unattractive,
The daughters of Yisrael are beautiful,
So too here the meaning is
that Hashem, blessed be He, will adorn them with ornaments;
for in truth our will is to do Your will,
רַק הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה מְעַכֵּב (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א),
only the leaven in the dough holds us back (Berachos 17a);
and then they will not be poor and unattractive.
עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מָחוֹל וְכוּלֵּי,
In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance, etc.,
and each and every one will point with his finger;
according to his grasp and comprehension of Hashem, blessed be He,
which he attained in this world.
And in the future, when he sees it explicitly,
he will point with his finger:
״הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה, קִוִּינוּ לוֹ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כה, ט).
"Behold, this is our God; we hoped for Him" (Yeshayahu 25:9).
